newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr finds little benefit in RBA silence.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr finds little benefit in RBA silence.

text.p: The Australian dollar remained in nervous consolidation at the midsession, holding above US$0.7410 support after the Reserve Bank of Australia left rates steady, but unable to rally while a cut remained a possibility.

While the RBA did not cut rates on Friday after Thursday's weaker than expected June employment figures, the market view is that there still will be at least one more interest rate cut, and this is proving a very effective cap on the dollar.
By 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT) the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7430/35, up on an opening US$0.7416/21 and a local close on Thursday of US$0.7425/30.

In early trade it had traded above US$0.7410 support. This has proved solid support through the week, and traders said there was good buying volume on dips here, consistent with rumours of an Asian player protecting an options postion.
The dollar had traded as high as US$0.7440 as the dollar gained some strength after the RBA remained silent at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT), the time it would announce any changes to policy.

However, gains were capped by selling into the rally. Local sentiment still favours another rate cut in the next few weeks, either after second quarter inflation and wages data on July 23 and 24, or after the RBA board next meets on August 5.

"The economy is running way below potential, there is no risk of inflation coming through, the labour market is very weak and there are just no wage pressures in the economy, so at this stage there's no reason why they shouldn't cut rates by another 50 basis points sometime in the next month or so," Citibank Australia senior economist Stephen Koukoulas said.
Adding to the pressure on the Australian dollar has been the recent lacklustre performance of commodities, analysts said.
May housing finance data released this morning and showing an 8.4 percent, slightly larger than market expectations, had little impact.
Although large, the fall followed a 12.2 percent rise, and the Bureau of Statistics cautioned that the data may be affected by the fact Easter fell earlier than usual this year.
On the crosses, the dollar was firmer. By 12.30 p.m. it stood at 84.35/45 yen from an early 83.83/93 and a Thursday close of 83.63/73.
In trade weighted terms, the dollar was at 56.7, up from a Thursday close of 56.6.
